items.standfirst: Democrat Mary Peltola has defeated incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan to complete a sweeping victory for the party in the Senate in the US midterm elections.
items.content: Democrat Mary Peltola has defeated incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan to complete a sweeping victory for the party in the Senate in the US midterm elections.

items.title: Mary Peltola unseats Sen. Dan Sullivan, giving Dems a 56-seat Senate majority
items.standfirst: It's the first time in 18 years a Democrat has won a Senate race in the state.
items.content: Former Rep. Mary Peltola ousted GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska — the first time in 18 years a Democrat has won a Senate race in the state.Her win gives Democrats a 56-44 edge in the Senate.Peltola was one of Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer’s top recruits for the cycle. She overpowered a Republican rescue mission for Sullivan and allegations of misconduct against her from former staffers to flip a state President Donald Trump won by 13 points in 2024. Her victory continues the blue wave born from voters’ frustrations at high costs and the Trump administration.Peltola will return to Washington, where she will become the first Alaska Native to serve in the Senate after previously holding the same distinction in the House.Her campaign had projected confidence about her path to victory as the vote count dragged on in a far-flung, rural state with long grace periods for late-arriving ballots.But her win was not without tumult. Trump’s Department of Justice sued to try to stop the certification if Sullivan lost, claiming voters could be confused by his same-name challenger. The president went so far as to call for votes for retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan and another longshot candidate in the four-way, all-party contest to be transferred to the incumbent.The Justice Department also started probing efforts to recruit Dan J. Sullivan after a New York Times report suggesting members of Peltola’s campaign and Senate Democrats’ campaign arm were involved. Both had previously denied involvement.

clusters.title: South Korea tightens security for national exam over AI cheating scandal
clusters.neutral_headline: South Korea’s high-stakes university exams upended by AI cheating scandal

items.title: South Korea tightens security for national exam over AI cheating scandal
items.standfirst: More than 550,000 candidates sat South Korea’s Suneung university entrance exam under extraordinary security, after an AI cheating scandal in which a top scorer on a national tax accountant exam admitted using a hidden mini camera to send questions to an AI system. Authorities inspected students’ glasses, deployed thousands of extra supervisors and ordered stickers over every button on candidates’ clothing. A nationwide disaster alert was also sent to make even muted phones buzz, exposing any devices smuggled into exam rooms.

items.title: South Korea’s high-stakes university exams upended by AI cheating scandal
items.standfirst: South Korea has been gripped by revelations of AI-aided cheating, just days before more than half a million students are to sit high-stakes entrance examsThe integrity of South Korea’s career-defining university entrance exam has been thrown into doubt after the top scorer in a recent professional exam admitted using a concealed camera and AI to cheat.On Thursday, more than half a million people, mostly school students, are due to sit the exam, known as the suneung, at 1,312 centres across the country. The exam runs for a gruelling eight hours over a single day and determines which university a candidate can attend and, in turn, their future prospects. Continue reading...

items.title: Gaza: Israel launched new offensive on Nuseirat
items.standfirst: Israeli tanks have moved east of the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza, with witnesses reporting heavy shelling, gunfire and airstrikes as the Israeli military says it has launched an operation in a Hamas-controlled area. Strikes killed at least three people on Wednesday, and displaced families are fleeing again, saying there is no real ceasefire. Israel and Hamas accuse each other of breaking the truce in force since October 2025, while Gadi Eisenkot tries to form a government after inconclusive elections.

items.title: Waymo pulls driverless taxis from freeways across the US after California ban
items.standfirst: The autonomous driving company suspended driverless taxi rides on US highways days after California banned the vehicles on its own freewaysWaymo has stopped offering driverless taxi rides on freeways across the US indefinitely. The Alphabet subsidiary pulled its vehicles from highways nationwide after California banned them from freeways in response to recent traffic incidents.Waymo had allowed riders to hail its robotaxis for freeway rides in the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Miami and Austin. The California-based company offers rides on city streets in many other areas, including Las Vegas, Dallas and Denver. Those rides remain unaffected by suspended freeway service. Continue reading...
